title: The Tower of Babel
text:
The Book of Genesis says that after the great flood, the whole earth had one language and one way of speaking. As people moved east, they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.

They said to one another: come, let us make bricks and bake them hard. They used brick instead of stone and bitumen for mortar. Then they said: let us build ourselves a city, and a tower with its top in the heavens, and make a name for ourselves, so that we will not be scattered over the face of the whole earth. And they set to work together.

The Lord came down to see the city and the tower. The text has him observe that they were one people with one language, and that this was only the beginning of what they would do. Nothing they planned would now be impossible for them. So the Lord confused their language, so that they could no longer understand one another's speech.

Unable to understand each other, they stopped building the city. The Lord scattered them from there over all the earth, which was exactly what they had feared. The city was called Babel, the text explains, because there the language of the whole earth was confused.
lesson: A shared language is one of a group's greatest powers. When people stop understanding each other, even a great common project falls apart and the group scatters.
